title: DX initiative: iteration heatmap + signal contracts for SDKs/docs/quickstarts
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Objective: build an operational playbook and an iteration heatmap that tracks signal-level regressions and adoption metrics for the SDKs, docs, and quickstarts. This ticket covers ownership of the heatmap definition, instrumented events contract, dashboard KPIs, and the cadence for OKR-linked reviews.

Background: multiple DX initiatives currently run in parallel (onboarding funnels, quickstarts, SDK-localization). We lack a consistent, low-noise signal contract to detect regressions early (e.g., broken quickstarts, failing SDK auth flows, docs search drop-offs). Engineering has partial telemetry; product teams produce ad-hoc dashboards that are hard to compare across cycles.

Goals and success criteria:
- Define 8 canonical signals across SDKs/docs/quickstarts (install success rate, sample-app run-to-completion, first-generation latency, docs search CTR, quickstart completion, SDK usage within 7d, error-rate by route, SDK upgrade opt-in rate).
- Ship an "Iteration Heatmap" dashboard that surfaces weekly deltas for each signal (absolute delta + z-score) and flags regressions when two consecutive weeks exceed threshold.
- Implement a minimal event contract (schema + example payloads) and partner with ENG to guarantee 95% event coverage for new DX ships.
- Integrate heatmap with initiative OKRs so Product/Design/Eng receive a weekly summary before cycle reviews.

Proposed timeline and milestones:
- Week 1 (this ticket): finalize signal list and threshold rules; produce a Confluence spec and example payloads.
- Week 2: instrument missing events (ENG tickets ENG-56890, ENG-57412) and validate event volumes on staging.
- Week 3: build Grafana/Metabase heatmap prototype; iterate with Design for UX.
- Week 4: run pilot on two quickstarts and the JS/Go SDKs; collect feedback and update thresholds.
- Week 5: rollout to full DX initiative and add weekly digest automation to Slack/Email for OKR owners.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Fidelity vs. noise: fine-grained signals increase noise and alert fatigue. We will start with aggregated weekly signals and add drilldowns for high-signal regressions.
- Centralized pipeline vs. per-repo events: centralized (preferred) simplifies dashboards but requires infra work (ENG cost). Per-repo events are faster to implement but create slippery differences. We chose centralized with a scoped scope to DX-related events only.
- Detection thresholds: fixed percentage delta vs. statistical (z-score). We opted for a hybrid: fixed min delta + z-score to handle low-volume metrics.

Data sources and instrumentation details:
- SDK telemetry: SDK ping events and sample-app webhooks (ENG-56890). Payload examples and schema are attached in the Confluence link below.
- Quickstarts: completion events emitted by the quickstart runner; fallback to GH action logs if instrumentation missing (ENG-57412).
- Docs: search and page view events instrumented via analytics pipeline; include query text hash to avoid PII.

Ownership and cadence:
- PM owner: Diego Morales (this ticket).
- Eng leads: Priya Singh (SDK telemetry), Tomas Becker (quickstarts infra).
- Design: Mei Chen (dashboard UX).
- Weekly cadence: heatmap snapshot every Monday, automated digest to DX-OKR channel, and triage during Friday office hours.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: instrumentation lag delays heatmap rollout. Mitigation: prototype with sampled logs and add event coverage gating.
- Risk: too many false positives. Mitigation: include manual verification step before escalating to Exec.

Attachments and artifacts: links below include spec, mockups, and sample payloads.

Next steps (short term): finalize the 8 signals, circulate the event contract to ENG, create the two dependent ENG tickets for telemetry, and schedule a 30-minute design sync for the heatmap mockups.
comments: 2026-01-16 - Diego Morales: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence. Action items: finalize signals list and create ENG tickets for missing telemetry. Assigned to Priya and Tomas for instrumentation scope.

2026-01-20 - Priya Singh (engineer): Reviewed the proposed SDK payloads; suggested adding 'environment' and 'sample_app_id' to help dedupe events. Created ENG-56890 to add SDK 'run_complete' and 'install_success' events. Blocking: backlog for telemetry infra until 2026-02-01.

2026-01-28 - Mei Chen (design): Initial heatmap mockups uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/example/heatmap-mockups. UX suggestion: include small-multiple sparklines for each signal to show 8-week trend.
2026-02-03 - Diego Morales: Decided on hybrid threshold approach (min delta + z-score). Documented rationale in Confluence and updated the spec. Added ENG-57412 for quickstart runner instrumentation.

2026-02-10 - Tomas Becker (engineer): Pilot instrumentation deployed to staging for JS/Go SDKs. Verified event format and sample volumes (~1.2k events/day combined). Links: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/487.
2026-02-18 - Diego Morales: Built Grafana prototype using staging events. Shared dashboard in DX-OKR channel. Requested design feedback and threshold tuning from PM/Design/Eng owners.

2026-02-25 - Aisha Patel (PM): Reviewed heatmap and approved proceeding to pilot on quickstarts. Suggestion: add a 'false-positive guard' requiring engineer sign-off before escalating to Reliability team.
2026-02-28 - Diego Morales: Updated ticket with pilot plan; scheduled office hours for 2026-03-07. Next deliverable: production-ready heatmap + weekly digest automation.
